title: Genetic Algorithms
html:
A genetic algorithm (GA) evolves a population of candidate solutions: the fittest are selected to reproduce, their encodings are combined by crossover, and random mutation keeps diversity. It is stochastic beam search with sexual reproduction.

1
Encode
Represent each candidate as a string — bits, digits or a permutation. 8-queens: 8 digits, one row per column.
2
Initialise
Create a random population of N individuals.
3
Evaluate fitness
Score each individual (higher = better). 8-queens: non-attacking pairs, max 28.
4
Select
Pick parents with probability rising with fitness (tournament or roulette-wheel selection).
5
Crossover
Cut two parents at a random point and swap the tails → children combine traits.
6
Mutate
With small probability change a random gene — keeps diversity, explores.
7
Replace & repeat
The children form the next generation (often keeping the best few — elitism) until fit enough or out of time.

Crossover in one picture

Genes (row of the queen in each column)
Parent A3 2 7 5 | 2 4 1 1
Parent B2 4 7 4 | 7 5 5 2
Child3 2 7 5 | 7 5 5 2 — head of A, tail of B

Crossover helps when the encoding has meaningful building blocks — contiguous substrings that are good on their own (a well-placed group of queens). If genes interact randomly, crossover is just a big random jump.

StrengthWeakness
Needs only a fitness function — no gradients, works on discrete or weird spacesMany evaluations; slow compared with problem-specific methods
Population explores several regions in parallelMany knobs: population size, rates, selection pressure, encoding
Easy to paralleliseNo optimality guarantee; can converge prematurely
schedulingcircuit & antenna designneural architecture searchgame-level generationfeature selectionevolution strategies (CMA-ES)genetic programming
Watch out

Premature convergence: if selection is too strong or mutation too weak, the population becomes clones of one early good individual and stops exploring. Raise mutation, use tournaments of smaller size, or add diversity measures.

What are the main operators of a genetic algorithm?

Selection (fitter individuals reproduce more), crossover (combine parts of two parents) and mutation (random small changes). Elitism optionally copies the best individuals unchanged into the next generation.

How is a GA related to local beam search?

Both keep a set of states and favour good ones. A GA is stochastic beam search where successors are made by combining two parents (crossover) rather than modifying one.
